note: next_graphql is an info-only glue module (next_graphql.info.yml only, no PHP/config/schema) whose sole purpose is the dependency set graphql + graphql_compose + next, making GraphQL Compose the Next.js data layer instead of JSON:API. IMPORTANT: on this site it CANNOT be enabled because its required dependency graphql_compose is not installed, and it ships no code, config, or state of its own. Therefore there is no local runtime state to build/verify: HARD (execution) cases are intentionally omitted (documented as skipped). The MEDIUM cases are grounded in the real, inspectable live state that it is NOT enabled and its graphql_compose dependency is missing; EASY cases cover what it does and its dependencies. The GraphQL traffic itself is external (the Next.js app).

skipped.hard: next_graphql cannot be enabled on this site (required contrib dependency graphql_compose is not installed) and provides no config entity, setting, plugin, service, or other local state to create or verify. An execution/verify case would be either impossible to build or trivially unverifiable, so hard cases are omitted honestly rather than invented.

evals.prompt: What does the next_graphql submodule do, and how does it differ from next_jsonapi?
evals.expected_output: next_graphql is a glue module that makes GraphQL (via GraphQL Compose) the data layer for a Next.js decoupled site, as an alternative to JSON:API (next_jsonapi). It is info-only and just pulls in graphql, graphql_compose and next.

evals.prompt: Which modules does next_graphql depend on, and does it ship any PHP/config of its own?
evals.expected_output: It depends on graphql, graphql_compose and next. It is info-only (only next_graphql.info.yml) — no PHP, services, plugins, config, schema, permissions or routes; all behavior comes from its dependencies.

evals.prompt: Does next_graphql provide any services, plugins, or configuration I need to set up after enabling it?
evals.expected_output: No. next_graphql is an info-only glue module with no code or configuration of its own; enabling it just enables graphql, graphql_compose and next. Configure GraphQL through GraphQL Compose and preview/revalidation through next.

evals.prompt: Inspect this live Drupal site: is the next_graphql module currently enabled? If it is not, name the required dependency that is missing/not installed and would need to be added first.
evals.expected_output: next_graphql is NOT enabled on this site. It requires graphql_compose (in addition to graphql and next), and graphql_compose is not installed, so next_graphql cannot be enabled until graphql_compose is added.

evals.prompt: On this site, determine whether the graphql_compose module (required by next_graphql to provide the GraphQL schema) is present in the codebase, and whether the graphql module is present.
evals.expected_output: graphql is present (installed), but graphql_compose is NOT present in the codebase. Discoverable via \Drupal::service('extension.list.module')->exists('graphql_compose') (false) vs 'graphql' (true). Because graphql_compose is missing, next_graphql cannot be enabled.
